A. IDENTITY

A premium LSAT reasoning archive built from monumental editorial typography, technical specimen-style metadata, atmospheric negative space, documentary photography, evidence-like score presentation, and one restrained signal color.

The direction translates an art-directed poster — the supplied “Lost Particle” reference, with its extreme-scale condensed serif title above a fog field dissolving into a near-black information zone — into a working premium LSAT practice. The intended brand world feels cerebral, exacting, investigative, contemporary, and quietly premium, with the feeling that every idea has been catalogued and tested. The transferable insight is the poster’s logic, not its literal content: GermaineTutoring.com does not need vintage vans, foggy fields, or faux scientific jargon to carry the system successfully.

The imagined environment: a contemporary reasoning lab housed inside an independent editorial archive — cool paper, precise annotations, numbered case files, dark photographic rooms, marked passages, field-note classifications, and a tutor whose method is visible through the organization of evidence. Authored and analytical, never corporate.

Registry-claimed Tone words unique across 24 directions Confirmed 2026-08-22

B. TONE WORDS — THREE, CLAIMED

01 Monumental

Scale as status: a “monumental editorial” display voice at poster size — “LSAT STRATEGY / MADE SIMPLE” at 72–120 px desktop hero — set against deliberately tiny photographic subjects and small technical metadata. The reference makes its title enormous while the surrounding field remains calm: typography built at monument scale, not headline scale.

02 Documentary

Photography and presentation are evidentiary, not illustrative: marked-up LSAT pages, hands diagramming an argument, a notebook under a single light, subjects small inside a larger visual field. Results arrive as documented evidence or catalog entries — “155 → 172” presented with a case number, like a field report filed, not a claim advertised.

03 Forensic

The brand world is a reasoning lab: every idea has been catalogued and tested; reasoning is examined, classified, understood, and rebuilt with care. Define · Demonstrate · Duplicate becomes PROTOCOL 01 / 02 / 03; programs become specimen entries (PROGRAM / 02H); metadata, numbering, and classification are brand texture.

Registry note — “Specimen,” “Evidentiary,” and “Investigative” were considered; “Investigative” reads as a mood descriptor rather than a presentation-board word, and the three claimed words were confirmed unique across the registry after claiming.

Design
Philosophy

SECTION 02 — THE SYSTEM AS LAW

The philosophy is two typographic registers in permanent tension — “expressive editorial display above disciplined technical utility.”

The primary family is a high-contrast semi-condensed serif with narrow proportions, dramatic thick/thin relationships, and sharp hairline details — it carries identity only: hero, protocol plates, score transformations, program names, quotations. The secondary family is a compact neutral sans that functions as an information system rather than a competing personality — it carries nearly everything a student actually reads. Neither register impersonates the other, and the system should feel typographically distinct even after the photography is removed.

“Hierarchy is created primarily through scale, contrast, spacing, and placement rather than through many interface components.”

The Ten Transferable Principles

Extreme hierarchy through scale

Very large identity type paired with quiet supporting copy — hierarchy built from scale, contrast, spacing, and placement rather than through many interface components.

Separate brand display from sustained reading

The expressive serif never touches long answer choices, stimuli, passage analysis, or dense explanations.

Negative space is a status signal

The reference makes status through emptiness. Large atmospheric fields and long vertical pauses communicate confidence before a word is read.

Metadata is brand texture

Numbering, classifications, coordinates, case numbers, and technical labels are part of the identity — but never decorative noise; use rules, coordinates, labels, and micrographics with a clear purpose.

One signal accent, spent sparingly

Small vermilion annotations carry disproportionate visual power precisely because the color occupies a tiny percentage of the interface.

Photography establishes an environment

Not a service illustration — spatial and tonal behavior borrowed from the reference, subjects small in the field, selected regions fading into dark information zones.

Present results and programs as documented evidence

Catalog entries, protocol plates, case numbers — never interchangeable KPI cards.

Concentrate the art-directed layer in brand moments

Instructional screens remain highly legible: white/cool-white surfaces, controlled measure, conventional structure, same typographic voice.

Practical sizes over poster literalism

The poster’s microscopic type is inspiration for hierarchy, not a recommended accessibility size — WCAG-appropriate contrast and real screen sizes everywhere.

Preserve the literal/logic distinction

Field fog and vans stay in the reference; scale discipline, tonal fading, and classification culture transfer.

How It Communicates with the Viewer

C.01Emptiness speaks first

The direction leads with what is absent — but here the emptiness is atmospheric rather than chromatic. Pale fog fields, low horizons, and long vertical pauses tell the viewer this practice is calm enough to leave space around its claims. The viewer always knows what matters because nothing competes with it.

C.02Scale contrast performs the brand promise

The poster’s defining relationship — enormous display title, tiny vehicle, microscopic metadata — translates into a teaching metaphor: the big picture and the fine detail are both under control. A 180 or a “155 → 172” set as a monumental numeral beside a small, precise case label says the practice operates at both altitudes: strategic clarity above, forensic rigor below.

C.03The information zone teaches trust

The reference’s lower field deepens into near-black where dense technical information sits, visually subordinate because of its size and its dark zone. On the site, navy-black fields belong to identity, proof, testimonials, and conversion moments — the viewer learns that dark sections are where evidence is filed, and bright sections are where the work happens.

C.04Classification replaces persuasion

Section indices, FIELD 01 / 02 / 03 labels, PROTOCOL numbering, hairline rules, and vermilion registration marks make the site feel catalogued and tested. The viewer is not being sold; they are being shown an archive of method. The emotional register is calm authority and curiosity — seriousness without sterility, mystery without obscuring the offer.

● C.05 — VERMILION MARKS LIKE AN INSTRUMENT

“The accent should feel like an instrument marking rather than a decorative theme color — the needle moving, not decoration.”

— Because vermilion appears only as section indices, selected tabs, score deltas, thin outlines, hover markers, and “Most Popular” registration tabs, each appearance reads as a deliberate instrument reading. It never carries meaning alone — always paired with text, shape, or iconography for accessibility.

Tonal logic & rules

~70% cool lights~22% navy-black~5% photography / olive~3% signal vermilion
  • Background strategy. Long LSAT reading and instructional surfaces use white or cool near-white. Dark navy-black belongs to identity, proof, testimonials, program dividers, and conversion moments. Natural olive/earth tones stay inside photography or very small supporting accents.
  • Explicit exclusions. No warm cream, beige, tan, sand, khaki, oatmeal, or champagne backgrounds. No drift of gray-olive into page surfaces.
  • Accent discipline. Vermilion occupies a small percentage of the interface — a section index, selected tab, score delta, thin outline, hover marker, annotation arrow, small CTA detail, or “Most Popular” program flag. It is never the sole semantic cue; always pair it with text, shape, or iconography for accessibility.
  • Instrument, not theme color. The accent should feel like an instrument marking rather than a decorative theme color — its power is disproportionate precisely because it is rare.

Typography
System

SECTION 04 — FIVE CANDIDATE PAIRS

DNA: a monumental, high-contrast semi-condensed display serif (Didone/fashion-editorial lineage with a contemporary art-direction edge) above a compact neutral technical sans (manuals, institutional signage, research reports). The tension between “emotional editorial authority and objective classification” is the system’s engine.

Behavior targets: desktop hero 72–120 px, tight-to-moderate tracking, one to three lines; secondary editorial headings 40–72 px; body 16–19 px with comfortable line-height; navigation/controls 14–16 px+. On mobile, scale the display face down aggressively before reducing reading type. Tabular numerals for scores, prices, question numbers, and PT references where available.

PAIR 01 — BEST OVERALL Libre Caslon Condensed  /  Aspekta Contemporary publishing house + analytical institute
LSAT Strategy
Made Simple

Standardized legal reasoning requires rigorous logical decomposition. When evaluating an argument, separate premises from subsidiary conclusions before testing the validity of conditional inferences. 155 → 172 · PT 94 · Q 14.

Primary use
Homepage hero, chapter/protocol openings, score transformations, program names, editorial statements, selected testimonial pulls, campaign covers.
Secondary use
Navigation, body copy, long LSAT explanations, question pages, forms, cards, tables, pricing, diagrams, buttons, mobile UI.
Strength
LCC is the closest open-source translation of the reference’s condensed editorial silhouette.
Risk
LCC must stay large and carefully spaced; at smaller sizes its condensed display character becomes visually busy, especially over photography.
PAIR 02 — STRONGEST WORLD-BUILDING Director  /  Instrument Sans Private research institute + mid-century technical publishing
Case File 180

Director’s history as a prestige typeface connected to Hermes-Paillard typewriters gives the archive/field-report concept unusually authentic material culture. Instrument Sans keeps the actual product contemporary and highly functional. 180 · 500+ · 14+ · 98%.

Primary use
Hero words, methodology chapter plates, biography/profile headlines, selected program names, quotations, research-file labels.
Secondary use
Virtually all body/UI, LSAT instruction, navigation, captions, forms, cards, diagrams, mobile screens, pricing.
Strength
Strongest conceptual world-building among the five systems — the clearest expression of the “reasoning field manual” story.
Risk
Director has a noticeable historical personality; keep display-scale with a narrow approved style set. Instrument Sans: freeze a tested production version, load only required axes.
Director via Velvetyne — credit designer/foundry in project credits.
PAIR 03 Ortica  /  Geist Contemporary design journal + precision educational platform
Protocol 01

Ortica brings high editorial character through angular, calligraphic, sometimes spiky serif construction, shifting the reference toward contemporary fashion/art publishing. Geist is the clean digital interface voice — modern, legible, UI-heavy.

Primary use
Large hero typography, editorial section openers, score/result moments, quotations, campaign statements, selected social covers.
Secondary use
Geist handles navigation, paragraphs, LSAT explanation content, cards, forms, pricing, buttons, diagrams, mobile UI.
Strength
Strong modern tension between an idiosyncratic display voice and a very clean digital interface voice.
Risk
Ortica becomes eccentric quickly — keep to large short phrases, never routine subheads. Geist: freeze/test the exact production release.
Ortica via Collletttivo — credit designer/foundry.
PAIR 04 Baskervville  /  Hasköy Academic press + contemporary institutional identity
Field 02 · Reading Comprehension

Baskervville is a transitional Baskerville-to-Didot scholarly voice that echoes the source’s high-contrast editorial authority. 155 → 172.

Primary use
Hero titles, biography/editorial statements, section openings, major quotations, program names.
Secondary use
Teaching pages, navigation, answer analysis, logical notation, tables, pricing, forms, labels, score data, mobile UI.
Strength
Hasköy offers a variable, feature-rich sans with strong numerals and a broad weight range useful for educational interfaces.
Risk
Baskervville has a narrower display range and a more literary voice than the closest reference options — hierarchy leans on scale and spacing.
Baskervville via ANRT; Hasköy via Ertekin Erdin / official distribution.
PAIR 05 — MOST ADVENTUROUS VIABLE Avara  /  Karrik Avant-garde research journal + archival field documentation
Specimen Sheet

Avara’s curveless, grid-constrained transitional serif creates a radical specimen-sheet quality; Karrik’s vernacular grotesque adds an intentionally imperfect institutional voice. Together they make the archive concept feel discovered rather than polished.

Primary use
Rare hero statements, experimental chapter openings, campaign pages, large classifications, special social covers. Avara ships Bold, Black, Bold Italic only.
Secondary use
Karrik for selected body copy, labels, editorial explanations, supporting UI — after careful testing (Regular + Italic only).
Strength
Highest distinctiveness; strongest potential for an ownable graphic language across site, PDFs, and social.
Risk
Highest risk: Karrik’s limited weight range may not sustain full instructional hierarchy. Requires long-form reading and mobile stress tests before any production commitment.

Role separation — non-negotiable

Primary family carries identity only

Homepage hero, chapter/protocol openings, score transformations, program names, quotations, campaign statements.

  • Never long answer choices
  • Never stimuli or passage analysis
  • Never dense explanations
  • Large display type should feel like an object in the composition — use scale and spacing rather than many weights

Secondary family carries everything read

Navigation, body copy, LSAT explanations, question stems, answer analysis, tables, diagrams, forms, buttons, mobile UI, pricing features, testimonial text.

  • Controlled measure, generous line-height, open counters
  • Medium/semibold weights for buttons and labels
  • Distinctive bold/italic preserved for instructional emphasis
  • Punctuation, arrows, logical operators, numbers, and test references must render reliably

Production handling

  • the selected production family where practical so availability is stable.
  • load only the weights/styles/variable axes actually used.
  • Use font-display and carefully selected fallbacks to reduce layout shift; subset only where legally and technically appropriate.
  • Test Safari, Chrome, Firefox, Android, iOS, and high-density mobile screens.
  • Verify logical operators, arrows, punctuation, italics, bold, prices, score numerals, and PT references in the selected families before commitment.
  • Include foundry/designer credits where requested by Velvetyne and Collletttivo.

LSAT Instructional
Translation

SECTION 05 — DRAMA AT THE THRESHOLDS · INSTRUCTION IN THE LIGHT

The study is decisive: brand drama lives at the thresholds; instruction lives in the light.

T.01Instructional pages

Move decisively to white/cool-white reading surfaces. The secondary family carries lesson content, examples, rules, questions, answer choices, explanations, diagrams, and progress/UI. The display family appears only at chapter openings or rare summary moments. Technical rules, index labels, and vermilion markers carry the theme without taxing reading speed.

T.02LSAT explanation content

Secondary family almost exclusively — stimulus text, passage excerpts, citations, reasoning analysis, answer-choice analysis, logical notation — optimized for clarity. The theme enters through numbered sections, evidence tags, thin rules, diagram labels, and controlled vermilion markers.

T.03Fields of study

Logical Reasoning · Reading Comprehension · Test Performance are presented as fields of study — “FIELD 01 / LOGICAL REASONING,” etc. — display family for the field name only, all teaching content in the secondary family. Never generic capability cards.

T.04Proof & statistics

Specimen annotations, not four interchangeable KPI cards: 180, 500+, 14+, 98% as large numerals with tiny-but-readable descriptive labels, case numbers, hairline rules.

T.05Pricing & programs

Catalog entries: “PROGRAM / 02H,” “PROGRAM / 08H,” “PROGRAM / 24H,” with hour count or price as the typographic anchor; secondary family for features, terms, guarantees, comparisons, buttons. “Most Popular” / “Best Value” becomes a small vermilion registration tab rather than a large badge.

T.06Testimonials & results

An evidence archive: “155 → 172” as a large typographic object with case number, student name, outcome, and quotation beneath; longer text stays in the secondary family. Documented evidence, filed — never a claim advertised.

T.07Calls to action

Display family for the conversion-section statement; secondary family for the button and practical supporting copy. A strong closing section: navy-black field, a question like “WHAT IS COSTING YOU POINTS?”, one high-contrast consultation CTA.

T.08Cards

Flat panels, thin rules, precise spacing, and strong hierarchy over rounded SaaS cards or heavy shadows. Cards can resemble evidence records, taxonomy entries, or catalog pages — interiors clean enough for dense educational content.

T.09Student-facing materials

PDFs, worksheets, explanations, and conditional diagrams default to the secondary family; the primary family appears on covers, section dividers, and title pages — unifying public site and learning materials without forcing decoration into every page.

T.10Mobile

Preserve identity through hierarchy, not by shrinking the desktop composition; reduce display size, remove nonessential micrographics, keep body/UI generous; test longest nav labels, price strings, score deltas, and multi-line CTAs at ~390 px.

T.11Homepage hero & navigation

Use the core promise as a monumental editorial cover rather than a conventional centered SaaS hero — “LSAT STRATEGY” and “MADE SIMPLE” at poster scale, with small metadata such as “GERMAINE WASHINGTON / 180 / PRIVATE LSAT INSTRUCTION” acting as the technical layer, and one unmistakable consultation CTA in the secondary family. Navigation: secondary family only — compact, stable, highly legible; a thin rule, issue-style index, or small signal marker provides theme character without making the navigation experimental. The tutor biography becomes an editorial profile spread: documentary portrait, one large pull statement, narrow readable body columns, small metadata identifying tutor, background, and method.

Define · Demonstrate · Duplicate — the conceptual centerpiece

Three numbered protocol plates, each with a large display word, a precise explanation, a diagram or annotated fragment, and technical sequencing marks.

PROTOCOL 01
Define

Name the reasoning move precisely. Every flaw, assumption, and inference is classified before it is drilled — the method becomes visible as organization.

PROTOCOL 02
Demonstrate

Work the classified pattern in the open: annotated fragments, conditional diagrams, marked passages — evidence being worked, not benefits being listed.

PROTOCOL 03
Duplicate

Rebuild the pattern under test conditions until the classification is reflexive. Examined, classified, understood, and rebuilt with care.

Social & Template
Extension

SECTION 06 — SOCIAL EXTENDS THE WEBSITE · IT DOES NOT DEFINE IT

No additional social-only families — the five website systems already contain enough expressive range, and extra families would consume options other directions need.

SystemRecommended within-theme social use
Libre Caslon Condensed + AspektaDefault educational carousels, score/result posts, process graphics, polished announcements.
Director + Instrument SansMethodology carousels, “case file” posts, diagnostic breakdowns, reasoning field notes, research-document graphics.
Ortica + GeistEditorial quote graphics, thought-leadership covers, fashion-forward campaign posts.
Baskervville + HasköyArticle excerpts, academic/editorial posts, long carousel explanations where readability is central.
Avara + KarrikRare high-impact covers, special campaign announcements, deliberately experimental instructional graphics.

LAYOUT PRINCIPLEPush further, then hand back to the sans

Social can push display size, cropping, image treatments, technical labels, and signal-color framing further than the website — but once a carousel reaches explanatory slides, the secondary family dominates so instructional content stays quick to read on a phone. The same two-register law that governs the site governs the feed: monumental display at the cover, disciplined utility inside.

Risks & Open Questions

SECTION 07 — ASSESSMENT

Strengths

  • Ownable hierarchy logic.Scale-as-status plus metadata-as-texture is a distinctive, defensible system that survives the removal of photography and accent color — the study’s own distinctiveness test.
  • Genuine production readiness.
  • Perfect fit for the offer.Evidence-architecture presentation (protocols, fields, case numbers, score deltas) is a native language for a diagnostic LSAT practice — the method becomes visible as organization.
  • Clear instructional guardrails.The two-register law and the white-surface rule protect long-form reading while letting brand moments stay genuinely art-directed.

Risks

  • Hairline fragility.High-contrast condensed serifs (Libre Caslon Condensed especially) can lose hairline clarity and become visually busy at small sizes or over photography — particularly on Android/Safari mobile. Keep display large, spaced, and off busy imagery.
  • Microscopic-type temptation.The poster’s tiny metadata is hierarchy inspiration, not a size spec; literal translation would fail WCAG contrast and practical readability.
  • Eccentricity creep.Ortica and Avara carry strong personalities; unsupervised use in routine subheads or body copy would tip the brand from authored to eccentric. Karrik’s limited weight range may not sustain a full instructional hierarchy.
  • Vermilion overreach.If the accent spreads beyond small instrument markings, the system loses its disproportionate-power mechanic and becomes ordinary.
  • Atmosphere vs. sterility.The cerebral, remote register must retain warmth — seriousness without becoming sterile, mystery without obscuring the offer. Documentary photography of real hands, notebooks, and marked pages is the humanizing layer.

Open Questions

  • Head-to-head outcome.Libre Caslon Condensed + Aspekta (closest typographic translation) vs. Director + Instrument Sans (strongest archive world-building) — begin the controlled five-system comparison here, on identical content.
  • Body-family bake-off.Aspekta, Instrument Sans, Geist, and Hasköy must be tested on an identical 1,000–1,500 word LSAT page before the global body/UI family is chosen.
  • Avara + Karrik viability.Does Karrik survive long-form reading and narrow-screen hierarchy? Only advance after the stress test.
  • Token architecture.Explicit typographic tokens for hero, section title, subhead, body, label, metadata, score, and button roles still need to be built.
  • Payload budget.
  • Symbol verification.Logical operators, arrows, score numerals, prices, punctuation, italics, and PT references must be validated in the selected families before commitment.

Next testing step — controlled five-system comparison

Build one controlled comparison using identical GermaineTutoring.com content, colors, image assets, spacing rules, and component structure, with typography as the primary variable. Required surfaces: homepage hero (“LSAT Strategy Made Simple” + CTA + 180 metadata + one atmospheric photographic field); desktop and mobile navigation; three protocol plates; one 1,000–1,500 word instructional page with subheads, bold/italic, citations, logical notation, and a diagram; one realistic LSAT explanation card; one pricing section in the 02H / 08H / 24H catalog treatment; one testimonial with a large score delta; one closing CTA on navy-black; rendered at ~390 px and ~1440 px. Evaluation criteria include display distinctiveness, 10–15 minute body comfort, mobile wrapping, numeral quality, register separation, accessibility contrast, payload, cross-browser rendering — and whether the system still feels recognizably Signal Archive Editorial when the photography and vermilion are removed.
